steps.context: Interpretive layer on the primary contrast. Human adipose tissue, treated vs control. Enrichment cannot carry the conclusion at n=12 and is included to describe the direction of the signature, not to establish it.
steps.question: Which hallmark and GO biological-process gene sets are enriched among the genes changing between treated and control adipose samples?
constraints: Use human gene-set collections only — the data is Homo sapiens adipose tissue
Use the tested-gene universe from T1S2 as the ORA background, not all annotated genes
Report unadjusted and BH-adjusted p-values; do not present nominal enrichment p-values as significant results
Do not re-run differential expression — consume the T1S2 results table
steps.description: Take the adjusted (~ sex + age + condition) DESeq2 results from T1S2. Run (a) over-representation analysis on the FDR<0.05 gene set, split into up- and down-regulated, against the universe of all tested genes; and (b) GSEA on the full gene ranking by the apeglm-shrunken log2 fold change (or by the Wald statistic if shrinkage compresses the ranking), using the human hallmark gene sets and the human GO biological-process gene sets available as reference gene-set collections for Homo sapiens in this environment. Gene identifiers in the counts matrix are HGNC symbols and the reference collections are symbol-based, so join directly on symbol and report the match rate. Both the hallmark and GO-BP human collections are used, and the symbol match rate against each is reported
Redundant nested GO-BP hits are collapsed before reporting a headline number of enriched sets
Dot plots for the leading sets from each collection are saved
If the FDR<0.05 DE list from T1S2 has fewer than 15 genes, the step reports ORA as uninformative and relies on the ranked GSEA, stating this explicitly
If a required human gene-set collection is not resolvable in the environment, the step reports the missing collection by name and proceeds with whichever human collections are available

plan.title: Adipose treated vs control: variance partition + DE
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single-batch bulk RNA-seq experiment in human adipose tissue: raw Salmon gene-level integer counts (12,000 genes x 12 samples, gene symbols in column 1) with a 12-row metadata table carrying condition (6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired), sex (F/M) and age (years). The research question has two parts in a fixed order, so the plan follows that order.

Part 1 (T1S1) asks how much expression variance condition, sex and age each explain. That is a variance-components question, not a testing question, and it is answered per gene with variancePartition::fitExtractVarPartModel on log2-CPM values (voom-weighted), fitting ~ condition + sex + age with condition and sex as categorical and age as a continuous fixed effect. With n=12 and 3 explanatory variables (4 model df, 8 residual df) the fractions are estimable but noisy; the step must report the distribution of the per-gene fractions (median and IQR per variable, violin plot, top genes by each variable) and explicitly note that residual variance will dominate and that the fractions are descriptive, not tests. A PCA of the same log-CPM matrix with PCs regressed on condition/sex/age gives an independent, low-dimensional read of which covariate structures the data globally — useful because a variance fraction computed per gene can be large in aggregate yet invisible in the leading PCs, or vice versa.

Part 2 (T1S2) is the actual contrast. Because the variance partition step precedes it and may show sex and/or age carrying non-trivial variance, the DE model is specified in advance as DESeq2 with design ~ sex + age + condition, so the treated-vs-control contrast is adjusted for the two recorded covariates; a design ~ condition only model is run alongside purely to quantify how much the adjustment changes the result (gene overlap, LFC concordance), not to choose between them post hoc. n=6 vs 6 with 8 residual df supports this design but is close to the limit — the step must report dispersion estimates, independent-filtering behaviour and the number of DE genes at FDR<0.05, and must not silently drop the covariates. apeglm shrinkage gives usable effect sizes for ranking.

T1S3 puts the DE result in biological context with hallmark and GO-BP over-representation plus a GSEA on the full shrunken-LFC ranking, using the staged human MSigDB GMT files (gene symbols match the counts matrix row names directly, so no ID mapping is required). Enrichment is interpretive only; with 12 samples it cannot carry the conclusion, and the step is instructed to say so if the DE list is small. The tracks are sequential because each depends on the previous artifact.
